segments.transcript: So... But it's a very human artist perspective. So the... Which is why AI made music feels like it's skipping an important part of it. But then what do I know what AI feel, and what do I know what they go through?
Even the part about patience that I thought was a very human or the the part of the creative process that I value a lot.
Because actually the unpredictability or the accidents and mishaps. Thing when things don't go right
and
you struggle with it, or you can't come up with something and the time you spend trying to get there, to me that's where the magic happens in song... In music making.

But but I I heard that, I forgot which AI company did this, but they tweaked the the response time Mhmm. Of AI to wait a bit Mhmm. Before they answer. And that... Didn't that really increase the quality of the response?
So actual... So that I find very interesting too. Like, these things, that we think are or that I I thought was a human thing can...
More and more, it's being implemented in in how AI function, I guess.
And this kind of patience waiting time, would you describe this as silence?
Does music ultimately comes from silence?
Yes.
I... Well, it's almost like... Well, I I think music changes the...
It's more... I I like to compare music to architecture because I feel like we're carving out space for something to exist.
It's like the the dark matter that we don't know about or that we can't detect with our senses yet, yet or ever, I guess.
But if you could, if you... It's possible. You could throw in every sound in the universe, in the world, every note on any scale, every scale into a song, but that sounds horrible.

And the more the more refinement you can put into it comes from what... It's important what you take out. What you take out is as much or leave out is, I think, actually even more important than what you put in.

And the space, like, if you're mixing a song, it's it's... That's a very physical process. You're sorting out the frequencies to make room for some frequencies to stand out here and some to stand out here. There's too much of this low frequency here. Let's cut that out. So it's really like, thinking it's a it's a spatial Mhmm. Thing as well.
And well, I I think is the true... Saying this true with language. What you don't say sometimes holds a lot more meaning than what you imply, I guess, in a poetic sense especially.
But yes, so the silences in between, just doesn't say like a bass pattern goes.
Where the sound exists is very important, but what makes the groove is the little moments of silence in between.
So I really... And a song, if you... I think the silence after a piece of music is somehow... It has been altered from the silence that preceded that song.
But that's how I I feel.
So I... Yeah. I think silence is very, very important.

What I was wondering again, it goes back to what we discussed in the beginning, whether the creative process is kind of something emerging inside... Out of silence, or is it like lots of noise that's like we are, you know, like like a piece of marble that you you you take out all the unnecessary
bits, and then you're left with the statue.
So do we have, like, this huge, huge noise inside us that we just take out parts of it until we are left with the text or with the music or whatever it is?
I I I don't know if it's...
I think there is definitely chaos. I feel like we...
There's just, like a... Lots of noise I guess basically.
